study_source_text:
# KO-reset snowball under flat Black-Scholes.
#
# The hard part of this payoff is a REGIME SWITCH. The trade runs a pre-KI KO
# schedule (barrier 103) to maturity_pre; only once it knocks in at 80 does it
# switch to a second, lower KO schedule (barrier 95) running on to
# maturity_post. Two value surfaces therefore live on different horizons -- and
# that is precisely what both deterministic engines got wrong before audit #13,
# maturing the not-yet-knocked-in surface on the post-KI schedule.
#
# Environment, economic scale and bounds are identical to snowball_flat_bsm and
# phoenix_flat_bsm on purpose: at multiplier 200, inception spot 100 and
# notional 20,000 the delta quantum and the reference move are both exactly
# 1.0, so a raw error IS a contract error and all three studies share one axis.
#
# Bound calibration (release procedure section 7, step 4). The cell gate needs
# the benchmark standard error inside 0.25 x 0.5 = 0.125 c. Measured at this
# budget (4 batches x 65,536 paths, paired bumps): pv 0.0110, delta 0.0087,
# gamma 0.0297. Gamma is the binding quantity at a 4.2x margin -- tighter than
# the other two studies, this being a longer-dated two-regime payoff -- but
# still compatible, and the sampler may take up to 32 batches to sharpen it.
#
# Offline study (minutes, not seconds). Run it with:
#   python -m quantark.modelvalidation run example/modelvalidation/ko_reset_flat_bsm.yaml
# Add --quick for a wiring check that is explicitly not bankable evidence.

study: ko-reset-flat-bsm
schema: 1

quantities: [pv, delta, gamma]

bounds:
  cell: 0.5
  mean_signed_bias: 0.1

sampling:
  paths_per_batch: 65536
  min_batches: 4
  max_batches: 32
  seed: 20260818
  bump: 0.01

economic_scale:
  builder: hedge_contracts
  params:
    hedge_multiplier: 200.0
    hedge_inception_spot: 100.0
    notional: 20000.0

environment:
  builder: flat_bsm
  params:
    spot: 100.0
    vol: 0.22
    rate: 0.025
    div_yield: 0.03

product:
  builder: equity.ko_reset_snowball
  params:
    initial_price: 100.0
    strike: 100.0
    maturity_pre: 1.0
    maturity_post: 2.0
    pre_ko_barrier: 103.0
    pre_ko_rate: 0.15
    post_ko_barrier: 95.0
    post_ko_rate: 0.03
    ki_barrier: 80.0
    ki_continuous: true
    contract_multiplier: 1.0

reference:
  builder: equity.ko_reset_snowball.mc_rqmc
  params: {}

candidates:
  - builder: equity.ko_reset_snowball.pde
    params: {accuracy: standard}
  - builder: equity.ko_reset_snowball.quad
    params: {grid_points: 1001}

cases:
  # At inception, clear of both KO barriers and well above KI.
  - {name: ordinary}
  # Just under the pre-KI KO barrier: the KO discontinuity sits inside the bump
  # stencil, where deterministic gamma usually breaks first.
  - {name: near_pre_ko, environment: {spot: 102.5}}
  # Just above the KI barrier: the regime switch is one small move away, so both
  # surfaces and the transition between them are in play at once.
  - {name: near_ki, environment: {spot: 80.5}}
  # Below the KI barrier: already knocked in at valuation, which exercises the
  # post-KI schedule and its lower KO barrier directly rather than through the
  # transition.
  - {name: below_ki, environment: {spot: 76.0}}
  # Low vol: the KI barrier is rarely reached, so almost all the value sits on
  # the pre-KI surface and its maturity must be exactly right.
  - {name: low_vol, environment: {vol: 0.12}}
  # Short horizons on both legs: few observations left and time discretization
  # error has nowhere to average out.
  - {name: near_expiry, product: {maturity_pre: 0.25, maturity_post: 0.5}}
  # Discrete KI monitoring instead of continuous. This is a different code path
  # in every engine -- the continuous one runs a Brownian-bridge correction that
  # the discrete one never touches -- so it is certified explicitly.
  - {name: discrete_ki, product: {ki_continuous: false}}
